LESSON: GUIDED WRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Writing 3.1 Guided writing (1 Lesson) (Punctuation) By the end of the sub-strand
Topic 3.2: Guided writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 1

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided writing, part of Writing 3.1 Guided writing (1 Lesson) (Punctuation) By the end of the sub-strand in Grade 4 GERMAN.

Key inquiry question: Why do you like writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. sketch and label a portrait of members of their nuclear family,

2. write down descriptions of members in their nuclear family, (z.B Meine Mutter ist 35 Jahre alt. Meine Mutter ist nett)

3. unscramble scrambled up names of nuclear family members,

4. fill crossword puzzles on nuclear family members collaboratively,

5. fill in blank spaces in incomplete texts on nuclear family members.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. sketch and label a portrait of members of their nuclear family,
2. write down descriptions of members in their nuclear family, (z.B Meine Mutter ist 35 Jahre alt. Meine Mutter ist nett)
3. unscramble scrambled up names of nuclear family members,
4. fill crossword puzzles on nuclear family members collaboratively,
5. fill in blank spaces in incomplete texts on nuclear family members.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Creativity and Imagination: The learner enhances their creativity when they sketch and label a portrait of members of

their nuclear family.

Values:
Love: The learner demonstrates their love of their family as they sketch and label a portrait of members of their nuclear

family.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: The learner develops an awareness of healthy filial relationships when they list members of their nuclear

family.

Link to other learning areas

The learner links the concept of nuclear family to the same concept in Religious Studies.
